commit.message:
fix: scope current-day settings reads/writes to the authenticated user

The `settings` document read in `GET /api/current-day` and the log-workout
auto-advance queried `SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.type='settings'` with no userId
filter and used an arbitrary cross-partition `settings[0]`. After the
MSAL -> auth.romaine.life migration left workout data (and a stale settings
doc) under a legacy `microsoft|...` userId, that stale doc (currentDay=1)
kept winning, so the app perpetually suggested Day 1 (Legs) even after Day 1
was logged.

- GET /api/current-day: dedupe by most-recent `updatedAt` and coerce to Number
- log-workout auto-advance: scope the settings lookup to `c.userId = req.user.sub`
  (partition-keyed), always upsert with `id = settings_<userId>` so a stray/legacy
  doc id can't spawn a duplicate, and coerce day comparison/increment to Number
- PUT /api/current-day: coerce incoming currentDay to Number so a string can
  never be persisted

Production data was separately consolidated onto the current auth.romaine.life
userId (duplicate settings docs collapsed to one, currentDay=2).
